summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier: no union-territory-specific trans law, enforcement series or incident pattern was found, and (not among the 12 states/UTs that constituted the mandated welfare board) its protective policy depends on the Union government, an RTI-documented driver of the welfare-board gap. No deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); assessed at the national score.

sources.summary: Human Rights Watch statement (26 March 2026) on India's 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill passed by parliament: removes self-identification, limits recognition to hijra/kinner and intersex categories, mandates medical certification, and adds offences carrying up to life imprisonment for "coercing or alluring" someone to be transgender. Directly Union-administered law in Dādra and Nagar Haveli and Damān and Diu; no territory-specific reporting.

BBC report (26 March 2026): both houses passed the amendment scrapping self-identification and requiring medical-board certification for recognition and surgery; protests, a Supreme Court-appointed panel's withdrawal request, presidential assent pending. As a Union Territory without its own legislature, Dādra and Nagar Haveli and Damān and Diu receives this framework wholly from the centre; the piece itself has no territory angle.

Times of India (Kolkata, 18 August 2024): alleged RPF "gender check" groping of a transwoman at a Kolkata metro station, denied with a counter-FIR. A West Bengal incident carried here only as a national datapoint on screening conduct toward gender-nonconforming people; no connection to Dādra and Nagar Haveli and Damān and Diu.
